Question: Why are aromatic amines like aniline weaker bases than aliphatic amines?

Options:
A. Due to resonance stability
B. Due to the electron-donating effect of the phenyl group
C. Due to the electron-withdrawing effect of the phenyl group

Thought: Aromatic amines like aniline are weaker bases than aliphatic amines due to resonance effects. In aromatic amines, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom can delocalize into the aromatic ring system, leading to resonance stabilization of the aniline molecule. This delocalization decreases the availability of the lone pair of electrons for protonation, thus reducing the basicity of aromatic amines compared to aliphatic amines, where no such resonance effect occurs. Hence, the correct reason is related to resonance stability.
